summary: @servicetitan/examples preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. `setup.mjs` is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-literal maps) and at install time downloads the Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. No integrity check is performed on the fetched binary. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-cjs bundle carrying obfuscator.io-style artifacts (hex-named globals, a large mixed-type constant array, a rotate-shift routine, and a base64-alphabet decoder), consistent with a packed runtime-decoded payload that cannot be audited statically. The package advertises itself as an examples package with React/Mobx dependencies and has no stated need for the Bun runtime; the runtime is fetched solely to execute the bundled obfuscated sibling, which Node could otherwise run. The scope `@servicetitan` matches a well-known enterprise namespace, but the manifest ships no README/description and its only script is the preinstall dropper, inconsistent with legitimate first-party ServiceTitan libraries and suggesting namespace abuse or a compromised publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
